To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the communities of soil macroinvertebrates and oribatids differed between agricultural meadow and heathland, that topsoil removal had a strong effect on soil fauna, and that macrofauna was very efficient in removing the litter layer from the soil surface in agricultural meadows, whereas it was less effective in heathland and topsoil removal sites.

the removal of the topsoil in restored heathlands leads to an increased similarity to the natural heathland in terms of soil macrofaunal communities but to a lower similarity with respect to soil microstructure and the community structure of soil microfauna.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of soil fauna on the development of soil properties and vegetation during the early stages of restoration of heathland from agricultural meadows.
the effects of the removal of topsoil and the resulting changes in soil fauna and soil structure on the restoration process of heathland ecosystems.
the effect of the removal of topsoil on soil macrofauna in the restoration of heathland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heathland restoration by topsoil removal is not a simple procedure and the effects of this procedure on soil biota, topsoil, and ecosystem functioning need to be considered.
the partial topsoil removal treatment was most similar to the original heathlands with regard to soil macrofauna community, topsoil structure and cellulose decomposition.
the restoration of the soil fauna community in topsoil removal heathlands is still in progress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

soil fauna communities and soil properties in the heathland plots were more similar after 15 years of restoration to those in the heathlands than to the agricultural meadows, but that the communities of soil fauna and soil properties in both the partial and the complete topsoil plots differed in some aspects from those in the heaths.
the partial topsoil removal treatment is a promising approach for restoration of heathlands, but the complete removal of the topsoil should be avoided.
the restoration success of heathlands is not only a function of the removal of the topsoil, but also of the presence of the soil fauna.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the restoration of heathlands from agricultural meadows is a long-term process, and the removal of topsoil is an important tool for the restoration of the soil fauna.
the removal of the topsoil layer from agricultural meadow soils to a depth of 10–15 cm, followed by the addition of heathland soil, is a viable approach for the restoration of heathland soils.

topsoil removal is an effective way to restore the heathland ecosystem, but that it may take several decades for the community composition of soil macrofaunal groups to recover to the levels observed in heathlands.
